wholePromptAnswerNoteAssessments.grammar: Singular question stem “Какое ... животное” agrees with singular answer “белый медведь”; the note is a complete, natural declarative sentence.
wholePromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: The correct option is the only listed species whose normal natural range is Arctic rather than Antarctic. FWS identifies polar bears with the Arctic sea-ice niche and ice-covered Northern Hemisphere seas. The note adds a concrete, useful ecological fact beyond the prompt and answer: sea ice is a platform for hunting seals.
wholePromptAnswerNoteAssessments.locator: FWS PDF L2-L6,L14-L18 (Arctic distribution); L199-L204 (sea ice used to hunt and feed on seals).

The note adds colony substrate and geographic detail, useful for distinguishing the option.

primaryFindings.claim: Polar bears use the Arctic sea-ice niche and occur across ice-covered seas of the Northern Hemisphere; sea ice is a platform from which they hunt seals.
Emperor penguins breed in colonies around the Antarctic continent; most are on fast ice.
Weddell seals have a circumpolar coastal distribution around fast ice and females pup there.
Adélie penguins live on the Antarctic continent and breed around its coast and on small rocky islands.

absoluteDifficulty.broadAdultGround: A single-step geographic recognition task: select one familiar animal that naturally belongs to the Arctic when the prompt explicitly contrasts the Arctic with Antarctica. No specialized zoological classification, dates, measurements, or multi-step inference is required. Distractors are familiar polar species and the notes make the distinction teachable.

taxonomyAndAntiOverlapGround.classification: Geography: natural range of named species across the Arctic/Antarctic region boundary. The learning target is spatial distribution, not biological taxonomy.
taxonomyAndAntiOverlapGround.antiOverlapGround: The Animals peer animals-polar-bear-arctic tests the feeding behavior of polar bears at seal breathing holes; this card tests where each named species naturally occurs. The Emperor-penguin winter-breeding peer tests seasonality, the penguin-flightless peer tests flightlessness, and the seal-flippers peer tests morphology. These related animal facts do not duplicate or reverse the region-distribution task.

The item tests species geographic distribution; actual order 10 defines a glacier by land location and gravity-driven motion. No duplication.
